sample_unit: neurologists (plus the AI system) evaluated on 5 clinical scenarios
models_evaluated: GPT-4 Turbo via Neura (Sciense) with dual-database retrieval architecture

links.outcome: Relevance and verifiability of AI-provided references, including hallucinated content
links.effect: All AI-provided references were classified as relevant with no hallucinatory content detected.
links.quote: All AI-provided references were classified as relevant with no hallucinatory content detected.

links.outcome: Normalized diagnostic score of AI versus neurologists on same cases
links.effect: AI achieved a significantly higher normalized score (86.17%) compared to neurologists (55.11%, p < 0.001). Differential diagnosis: 85% vs 46.15%; final diagnosis: 88.24% vs 70.93%.
links.quote: AI achieved a significantly higher normalized score (86.17%) compared to neurologists (55.11%, p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Curated domain-specific knowledge base with dual-database long-term/short-term memory architecture to improve LLM diagnostic performance

screen.reason: Evaluates a specialized LLM (GPT-4 Turbo with memory retrieval architecture) against neurologists on simulated clinical vignettes for diagnostic performance and hallucination rates.
